In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:
a) Unless specified differently in the relevant clause, all values and templates used in a basic program statement shall be completely initialized (for exemption see e.g. clause 19.1).

NOTE: Note that the restriction applies to component of statements defined in the present document, like the boolean condition of if statements, but not to the content of statement blocks embedded into the statements.
Values or templates may be assigned to variables or template variables (see clause 11).
This is indicated by the symbol ":=".
ValueRef ":=" ( Expression | TemplateBody )
During execution of an assignment, the right-hand side of the assignment shall evaluate to a value or template that is at least partially initialized.
The effect of an assignment is to bind the variable to the value of the expression or to a template.
Assignments use the rules of passing by value.
If the variable being assigned is of a type whose values are object references, only the reference is copied, but the referenced object (e.g. component, timer or port) is not.
In all other cases, the content being assigned shall be a copy of the evaluated right-hand side.
Assignments are processed from left to right, i.e. expressions in the left hand side are evaluated before those in the right hand side.
The evaluations obey the operator precedence defined in table 6.

Unless the assignment is to a lazy or fuzzy variable or parameter, the right hand side is evaluated completely before the resulting value or template is bound to the evaluated left-hand side of the assignment.
Whenever assignments are used within the right hand side of an assignment (due to assignment notation), these rules apply recursively.

A structured value on the right-hand side of the assignment shall be assigned completely to the variable on the left-hand side of the assignment, If a partially initialized value is assigned to a completely initialized variable, fields uninitialized at the right-hand side of the assignment shall also become uninitialized at the left-hand side.

When a direct or indirect element or field of a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned, the variable is also evaluated as much as necessary before assignment, i.e. if an ancestor of that element or field is initialized with a function call, it shall be evaluated.
Thus, if the variable is fully assigned, it does not need to be evaluated before assignment.

NOTE: If a sub-field or sub-element of a fuzzy variable is assigned that has an ancestor which was formerly assigned a function call, this function call will be evaluated once before the assignment and replaced by its result inside the variable.
Thus, the other sub-fields and sub-elements of that ancestor, apart from the field or element being assigned become non-fuzzy.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16, the following restrictions apply:
a) The right-hand side of an assignment shall evaluate to a value, template, port or timer which is type compatible with the variable at the left-hand side of the assignment.

b) When the right-hand side of the assignment evaluates to a template (global or local template, in-line template, template variable or a matching mechanism), the variable at the left hand side shall be a template variable.
c) The right-hand side of an assignment shall evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.

d) If the left-hand side of the assignment is a reference to a non-optional value object (i.e. a value definition, a mandatory field, a record/set of/array element, a union alternative, a value parameter), the right-hand side shall not be a reference to an omitted field or the omit symbol.
e) Using a reference to an omitted field in the right-hand side of the assignment has the same effect as using the
omit keyword.

In addition to the basic assignments it is possible to use shorthand assignments for integer variables that shall be incremented by 1 or decremented by 1.
The statement "v_integer++" is a shorthand form of "v_integer ;= v_integer + 1" and the statement "v_integer--" is a shorthand form of "v_integer := v_integer – 1".
var integer v_j; for (v_j:=1; v_j<=10; v_j++) { … }; // increments v_j after each iteration v_j--; // decrements the variable v_j
The if-else statement, also known as the conditional statement, is used to denote branching in the control flow.
NOTE 1: `else if "(" BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock [ else` _StatementBlock] is a shorthand notation for_ `else "{" if "(" BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock [ else` _StatementBlock] "}"._

NOTE 2: if "(" (VarInstance | Assignment) ";" BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock [else _StatementBlock] is a shorthand_ notation for **"{" (VarInstance | Assignment) ";" if "(" BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock [ else** _StatementBlock] "}"._
The branching of the control flow is decided upon the value of the Boolean expressions - the condition.
A statement block - and only one - will be executed, if its condition evaluates to true.
The optional else specifies a statement block that will be executed if all the "if" and "else if" conditions before are false.
Boolean expressions may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.
The scope of variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the if-statement, including its else branch.
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.
The select case statement is an alternative syntactic form of the if-else statement.

select "(" [(VarInstance|Assignment) ";"] SingleExpression ")" "{" 
     { case "(" { TemplateInstance[","] } ")" StatementBlock }+
     [ case else StatementBlock ]
  "}"
The select case statement is an alternative to using if .. else `if .. else statements when comparing a value to` one or several other values.
The statement contains a header part and one or more branches.
Never more than one of the branches is executed.
In the header part of the select case statement an expression shall be given.
The expression may be preceded by an _init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.
The scope of_ variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the select case statement.

Each branch starts with the case keyword followed by a list of templateInstance (a list branch, which may also contain a single element) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.
All templateInstance in all list branches shall be of a type compatible with the type of the expression in the header.
A list branch is selected and the statement block of the selected branch is executed only, if any of the templateInstance matches the value of the expression in the header of the statement.
On executing the statement block of the selected branch (i.e. not jumping out by a goto statement), execution continues with the statement following the select case statement.
The statement block of an else branch is always executed if no other branch textually preceding the else branch has been selected.
Branches are evaluated in their textual order.
If none of the templateInstance-s matches the value of the expression in the header and the statement contains no else branch, execution continues without executing any of the select case branches.
NOTE 1: In general, it cannot be decided if templateInstances overlap or not.
However, it is advised to use in the branches templateInstances that don't overlap.
In such situations tools might provide better runtime performance.
The handling however is tool-specific.
NOTE 2: When more than one branch could be selected (the templateInstances overlap) the textually first will be selected.
For this reason overlapping is discouraged, handling however is tool-specific.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16, the following restrictions apply:

a) The select _SingleExpression and the case TemplateInstance-s shall be type compatible._ b) When all templateInstances of all branches can be statically evaluated in compile time to specific values or value ranges no two branches shall match the same value.
To allow easier usage of the select statement for values of union types or anytype, a special form of the select statement exists.

select union "(" [(VarInstance|Assignment) ";"] SingleExpression ")" "{" 
     { case "(" ({ Identifier [","] } | { TypeIdentifier [","] }) ")" StatementBlock }+
     [ case else StatementBlock ]
  "}"
The statement contains a header part and one or more branches.
Never more than one of the branches is executed.
In the header part of the select union statement a template instance of union type or anytype shall be given.
The expression in the header may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.
The scope of variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the
select union statement.

If the template instance has a union type, each branch shall start with the case keyword followed by one or more identifiers of the alternatives (fields) of the union type (a list branch) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

If the template instance has type anytype, each branch shall start with the case keyword followed by one or more type names (a list branch) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.
The StatementBlock of the list branch containing the identifier or type identifier of the chosen alternative is executed.
If no case exists for the chosen alternative, the StatementBlock of the else branch, if it is present, is executed.
Otherwise, the select union statement has no effect.
a) The SingleExpression in the header of the select union statement shall be of a union type.
It shall be at least partially initialized.
b) Every Identifier in a case of the select union statement shall be an identifier of an alternative of the
union type of the template instance given to the statement's header.
c) No two cases in a select union statement shall have the same case Identifier or TypeIdentifier.
The traditional form of the for statement defines a counter loop.

for "(" ( VarInstance | Assignment ) ";" BooleanExpression ";" Assignment ")"
       StatementBlock
The for statement contains two assignments and a boolean expression.
The first assignment is necessary to initialize the index (or counter) variable of the loop.
The boolean expression terminates the loop and the second assignment is used to manipulate the index variable.
The value of the index variable is increased, decreased or manipulated in such a manner that after a certain number of execution loops a termination criteria is reached.
The termination criterion of the loop shall be expressed by a boolean expression.
It is checked at the beginning of each new loop iteration.

If it evaluates to true, the execution continues with the statement block in the for statement, if it evaluates to false, the execution continues with the statement which immediately follows the for loop.
If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt, alststep or interleave, then the loop is terminated, too.
The index variable of a for loop can be declared before being used in the for statement or can be declared and initialized in the for statement header.
If the index variable is declared and initialized in the for statement header, the scope of the index variable is limited to the loop body, i.e. it is only visible inside the loop body.
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.
The range-based loop iterates over the elements provided by a range expression.

for "(" [ var TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] ValueRef in Expression ")"
      StatementBlock
The range expression is evaluated once before beginning the loop and may be partially initialized.
The range _expression shall evaluate to a value with root type record of, set of, array, octetstring, hexstring, bitstring,_ **charstring or universal charstring.**
Elements are iterated in sequential order.
In each iteration the appropriate element is assigned to the iteration variable and the statement block is executed.
If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, its scope and lifetime is limited to the statement block, i.e. a new iteration variable is initialized in every iteration.
If the iteration variable is declared outside the for statement, after execution its value will be that of the last iteration.
The assignment to the iteration variable follows the rules specified in clause 19.1.1 with the exception that assignment of uninitialized elements is permitted.
When an uninitialized value is assigned to the iterator variable, the iterator variable becomes uninitialized.
NOTE 1: The iteration order of map keys and map values is tool dependent and is not guaranteed to be the same from one iteration to the next.
NOTE 2: The behaviour of lazy or fuzzy iteration variables is not specified and should not be used to avoid future compatibility issues.
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.

A while statement defines a loop that is executed as long as the loop condition holds.
while "(" [(VarInstance|Assignment) ";"] BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock
The loop condition may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.
The scope of variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the while statement.
The loop condition shall be checked at the beginning of each new loop iteration.
If the loop condition does not hold, then the loop is exited and execution shall continue with the statement, which immediately follows the while loop.
If a
break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt, alststep or interleave, then the
loop is terminated, too.
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.
while (v_j<10){ … }
A do-while statement defines a loop that is executed up until the loop condition does not hold.
do StatementBlock while "(" BooleanExpression ")"
The do-while loop is identical to a while loop with the exception that the loop condition shall be checked at the end of each loop iteration.
This means when using a do-while loop the behaviour is executed at least once before the loop condition is evaluated for the first time.
If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt, alststep or interleave, then the loop is terminated, too.
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.
do { … } while (v_j<10);
The label statement allows the specification of labels in test cases, functions and altsteps.
label LabelIdentifier
A label marks a statement.
The label is used by the goto statement (see clause 19.8) to transfer control to a labelled statement.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16, the following restrictions apply:

a) A label statement can be used freely like other TTCN-3 behavioural program statements according to the syntax rules defined in annex A. It can be used before or after a TTCN-3 statement but not as the first statement of an alternative or top alternative in an alt statement, interleave statement or altstep.
b) Labels used following the label keyword shall be unique among all labels defined in the same test case, function or altstep.
A goto statement performs a jump to a label.
goto LabelIdentifier
The goto statement can be used in functions, test cases and altsteps to transfer control to a labelled statement.

The goto statement provides the possibility to jump freely, i.e. forwards and backwards, within a sequence of statements, to jump out of a single compound statement (e.g. a while loop) and to jump over several levels out of nested compound statements (e.g. nested alternatives).
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16, the following restrictions apply:
a) It is not allowed to jump out of or into functions, test cases and altsteps.
b) It is not allowed to jump into a sequence of statements defined in a compound statement (i.e. alt statement,
while loop, for loop, if-else statement, do-while loop and the interleave statement).
c) It is not allowed to use the goto statement within an interleave statement.
The stop statement terminates execution of test components, a test case or a test control.
stop
The stop statement terminates execution in different ways depending on the context in which it is executed.
When executed in a control behaviour, it terminates the execution of the control component.
When invoked in a test case, altstep or function that are executed on a test component, it terminates the relevant test component.
NOTE: The semantics of a stop statement that terminates a test component is identical to the stop component operation self.stop (see clause 21.3.3).
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.
The return statement terminates execution of functions or altsteps.
return [ Expression | TemplateInstance ]
The return statement terminates execution of a function or altstep and returns control to the point from which the function or altstep was called.
When used in functions, a return statement may be optionally associated with a return value or template.
TTCN-3 allows optional statement blocks that may follow altstep calls within alt statements.
If there is a statement block, the return statement returns control to the beginning of this statement block and the statement block is executed before the alt statement is left.
If there is no statement block, test execution continues with the first statement following the alt statement.
The return value or template is first evaluated before returning.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16, the following restrictions apply:
a) The return statement shall not be present in testcase definitions.

The log statement provides the means to write one or more log items to some logging device associated with the test control or the test component in which the statement is used.
Items to be logged shall be identified by a comma-separated list in the argument of the log statement.
Log items may be individual language elements specified in table 18 or expressions composed of such log items.
It is strongly recommended that the execution of the log statement has no effect on the test behaviour.

In particular, functions used in a log statement should not (explicitly or implicitly) change component variable values, port or timer status, and should not change the value of any of its inout or out parameters.
NOTE: It is outside the scope of the present document to define complex logging and trace capabilities which may be tool dependent.

On executing a break statement the innermost, currently executed loop, alt statement or interleave statement is left.
Execution continues with the statement following the construct which is left.
Using break outside the body of a loop (for, while, do-while) or an alternative of an alt or interleave statement shall cause an error.
Altsteps are always executed within a surrounding alt statement.
If the execution of a top alternative of an altstep (see clause 16.2.1) ends with a break statement, the altstep and the surrounding alt statement are left.
Execution continues with the statement following the surrounding alt statement.
NOTE: TTCN-3 allows optional statement blocks that may follow altstep calls within alt statements.
These statement blocks are not executed when the altstep is left by executing a break statement.
A return statement has to be used, if such an optional statement block has to be executed (see clause 19.10).
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.
A continue statement causes the start of the next iteration of a loop.
continue
On executing a continue statement, the subsequent statements of the body of the innermost, currently executed loop are skipped and the next iteration starts.
Using continue outside the body of a loop (for, while, do-while) shall cause an error.
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.
Statement blocks can be used like basic program statements to introduce a local scope in the flow of control of TTCN-3 behaviour.
The declarations and statements in a statement block are executed in the order of their appearance, i.e. sequentially.
"{" { LocalDefinition | Statement } "}"
A statement block defines a local scope unit.
Scoping rules for TTCN-3 are defined in clause 5.2.
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment
requirements.canonical: The effect of an assignment IS to bind the variable on the left hand side to the value of the expression or to a template.
requirements.original: The effect of an assignment is to bind the variable to the value of the expression or to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment
requirements.canonical: An assignment uses the rules of passing by value.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment
requirements.condition: the variable being assigned is of a type whose values are object references
requirements.canonical: If the assigned variable is of a type whose values are object references, only the reference IS copied by the assignment and the referenced object (e.g. component, timer or port) IS NOT copied.
requirements.original: If the variable being assigned is of a type whose values are object references, only the reference is copied, but the referenced object (e.g. component, timer or port) is not.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment
requirements.condition: the variable is not of a type whose values are object references
requirements.canonical: If the assigned variable is not of an object reference type, the content being assigned SHALL be a copy of the evaluated right hand side.
requirements.original: In all other cases, the content being assigned shall be a copy of the evaluated right-hand side. If the variable being assigned is of a type whose values are object references, only the reference is copied, but the referenced object (e.g. component, timer or port) is not.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment
requirements.canonical: An assignment IS processed from left to right, i.e. expressions in the left hand side are evaluated before those in the right hand side.
requirements.original: Assignments are processed from left to right, i.e. expressions in the left hand side are evaluated before those in the right hand side.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment

requirements.subject: ent:right-hand-side
requirements.condition: the assignment is not to a lazy or fuzzy variable or parameter

requirements.original: Unless the assignment is to a lazy or fuzzy variable or parameter, the right hand side is evaluated completely before the resulting value or template is bound to the evaluated left-hand side of the assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment

requirements.original: Whenever assignments are used within the right hand side of an assignment (due to assignment notation), these rules apply recursively.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment

requirements.original: A structured value on the right-hand side of the assignment shall be assigned completely to the variable on the left-hand side of the assignment, If a partially initialized value is assigned to a completely initialized variable, fields uninitialized at the right-hand side of the assignment shall also become uninitialized at the left-hand side.

requirements.canonical: When a direct or indirect element or field of a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned, the variable SHALL be evaluated as much as necessary before the assignment, i.e. an ancestor of that element or field initialized with a function call SHALL be evaluated.
requirements.original: When a direct or indirect element or field of a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned, the variable is also evaluated as much as necessary before assignment, i.e. if an ancestor of that element or field is initialized with a function call, it shall be evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.condition: the lazy or fuzzy variable is fully assigned
requirements.canonical: If a lazy or fuzzy variable is fully assigned, the variable NEED NOT be evaluated before the assignment.
requirements.original: Thus, if the variable is fully assigned, it does not need to be evaluated before assignment. When a direct or indirect element or field of a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned, the variable is also evaluated as much as necessary before assignment, i.e. if an ancestor of that element or field is initialized with a function call, it shall be evaluated.

requirements.original: NOTE 2: if "(" (VarInstance | Assignment) ";" BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock [else _StatementBlock] is a shorthand_ notation for **"{" (VarInstance | Assignment) ";" if "(" BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock [ else** _StatementBlock] "}"._

requirements.subject: ent:if-else-statement
requirements.canonical: The branching of the control flow of an if-else statement IS decided upon the value of the boolean expressions (the conditions).
requirements.original: The branching of the control flow is decided upon the value of the Boolean expressions - the condition.

requirements.subject: ent:if-else-statement
requirements.canonical: Exactly one statement block of an if-else statement IS executed, namely the first one (in textual order) whose condition evaluates to true.
requirements.original: A statement block - and only one - will be executed, if its condition evaluates to true.

ambiguity.issue: The text does not state which block is executed when several conditions evaluate to true, nor that conditions are evaluated in order; chosen the conventional reading (first true condition in textual order), which follows from the shorthand in NOTE 1.
readings: Exactly one statement block IS executed, namely the first one in textual order whose condition evaluates to true.
At most one statement block IS executed, which is one whose condition evaluates to true (selection unspecified).

requirements.subject: ent:else-clause
requirements.condition: all preceding if and else if conditions are false
requirements.canonical: The statement block of the optional `else` branch IS executed if all preceding `if` and `else if` conditions are false.
requirements.original: The optional else specifies a statement block that will be executed if all the "if" and "else if" conditions before are false.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-expression
requirements.canonical: A boolean expression of an if-else statement MAY be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment).
requirements.original: Boolean expressions may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:init-statement
requirements.canonical: An init statement of an if-else statement IS executed before the boolean expression it precedes is evaluated.
requirements.original: Boolean expressions may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:init-statement
requirements.canonical: The scope of a variable declared within an init statement SHALL be limited to the if-else statement, including its else branches.
requirements.original: The scope of variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the if-statement, including its else branch.

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.canonical: The select case statement IS an alternative syntactic form of the if-else statement.
requirements.original: The select case statement is an alternative syntactic form of the if-else statement.

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.canonical: The select case statement has the syntax `select` "(" [(VarInstance | Assignment) ";"] SingleExpression ")" "{" followed by one or more list branches `case` "(" {TemplateInstance [","]} ")" StatementBlock, an optional else branch `case else` StatementBlock, and a closing "}".
requirements.original:
select "(" [(VarInstance|Assignment) ";"] SingleExpression ")" "{" 
     { case "(" { TemplateInstance[","] } ")" StatementBlock }+
     [ case else StatementBlock ]
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.canonical: The select case statement IS an alternative to nested if-else statements when comparing a value to one or several other values.
requirements.original: The select case statement is an alternative to using if .. else `if .. else statements when comparing a value to` one or several other values.

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.canonical: A select case statement IS composed of a header part and one or more branches.
requirements.original: The statement contains a header part and one or more branches.

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.canonical: An execution of a select case statement SHALL NOT execute more than one of its branches.
requirements.original: Never more than one of the branches is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:header-part
requirements.canonical: The header part of a select case statement SHALL contain an expression.
requirements.original: In the header part of the select case statement an expression shall be given.

requirements.subject: ent:init-statement
requirements.canonical: The expression in the header part of a select case statement MAY be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment).
requirements.original: The expression may be preceded by an _init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:init-statement
requirements.canonical: The init statement of a select case statement IS executed before the header expression is evaluated.
requirements.original: The expression may be preceded by an _init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: The scope of a variable declared within the init statement of a select case statement SHALL be limited to the select case statement.
requirements.original: The scope of_ variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the select case statement.

requirements.subject: ent:list-branch
requirements.canonical: A list branch of a select case statement IS the `case` keyword followed by a list of one or more template instances and a statement block.
requirements.original: Each branch starts with the case keyword followed by a list of templateInstance (a list branch, which may also contain a single element) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

ambiguity.issue: The text uses the BNF name 'templateInstance' instead of the term 'template instance'.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.canonical: The last branch of a select case statement MAY be an else branch consisting of the `case` keyword followed by the `else` keyword and a statement block.
requirements.original: Each branch starts with the case keyword followed by a list of templateInstance (a list branch, which may also contain a single element) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.canonical: An else branch SHALL only appear as the last branch of a select case statement.
requirements.original: Each branch starts with the case keyword followed by a list of templateInstance (a list branch, which may also contain a single element) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: Every template instance in a list branch of a select case statement SHALL be of a type compatible with the type of the header expression.
requirements.original: All templateInstance in all list branches shall be of a type compatible with the type of the expression in the header.

ambiguity.issue: The text uses the BNF name 'templateInstance' instead of the term 'template instance'.

requirements.subject: ent:list-branch
requirements.canonical: A list branch of a select case statement IS selected, and its statement block executed, only if at least one of its template instances matches the value of the header expression.
requirements.original: A list branch is selected and the statement block of the selected branch is executed only, if any of the templateInstance matches the value of the expression in the header of the statement.

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.condition: the statement block of the selected branch is executed without jumping out by a goto statement
requirements.canonical: When the statement block of the selected branch has been executed without jumping out by a goto statement, execution SHALL continue with the statement following the select case statement.
requirements.original: On executing the statement block of the selected branch (i.e. not jumping out by a goto statement), execution continues with the statement following the select case statement.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.condition: no textually preceding branch has been selected
requirements.canonical: The statement block of an else branch IS executed if no branch textually preceding the else branch has been selected.
requirements.original: The statement block of an else branch is always executed if no other branch textually preceding the else branch has been selected.

requirements.subject: ent:branch
requirements.canonical: The branches of a select case statement ARE evaluated in their textual order.
requirements.original: Branches are evaluated in their textual order.

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.condition: no template instance matches and there is no else branch
requirements.canonical: If none of the template instances matches the value of the header expression and the select case statement contains no else branch, execution continues after the select case statement without executing any branch.
requirements.original: If none of the templateInstance-s matches the value of the expression in the header and the statement contains no else branch, execution continues without executing any of the select case branches.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool CANNOT in general decide whether the template instances of a select case statement overlap.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: In general, it cannot be decided if templateInstances overlap or not.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The template instances used in the branches of a select case statement SHOULD NOT overlap.
requirements.original: However, it is advised to use in the branches templateInstances that don't overlap.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the template instances do not overlap
requirements.canonical: When the template instances of a select case statement do not overlap, a TTCN-3 tool CAN provide better runtime performance.
requirements.original: In such situations tools might provide better runtime performance.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: The handling of non-overlapping template instances in a select case statement IS tool-specific.
requirements.original: The handling however is tool-specific.

ambiguity.issue: 'The handling' has no clear referent; chosen reading: the performance optimisation for non-overlapping template instances is tool-specific.
readings: The optimisation of select case statements with non-overlapping template instances IS tool-specific.
The handling of overlapping template instances in a select case statement IS tool-specific.

requirements.subject: ent:select-case-statement
requirements.condition: the template instances of more than one branch match
requirements.canonical: When more than one branch of a select case statement could be selected because the template instances overlap, the textually first branch IS selected.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: When more than one branch could be selected (the templateInstances overlap) the textually first will be selected.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: Overlapping template instances SHOULD NOT be used in the branches of a select case statement.
requirements.original: For this reason overlapping is discouraged, handling however is tool-specific.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: The handling of overlapping template instances in a select case statement IS tool-specific.
requirements.original: For this reason overlapping is discouraged, handling however is tool-specific.

ambiguity.issue: Contradicts the preceding sentence of NOTE 2, which states that the textually first branch is selected; chosen reading: only tool optimisation is tool-specific.
readings: Selection of the textually first matching branch IS mandated; only the internal optimisation IS tool-specific.
Which branch IS selected for overlapping template instances IS tool-specific.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression in the header of a select case statement and every case template instance SHALL be type compatible.
requirements.original: a) The select _SingleExpression and the case TemplateInstance-s shall be type compatible._

requirements.subject: ent:branch
requirements.condition: all template instances can be evaluated at compile time to specific values or value ranges
requirements.canonical: If all template instances of all branches of a select case statement can be statically evaluated at compile time to specific values or value ranges, two branches SHALL NOT match the same value.
requirements.original: b) When all templateInstances of all branches can be statically evaluated in compile time to specific values or value ranges no two branches shall match the same value.

requirements.subject: ent:select-union-statement
requirements.canonical: The select union statement IS a special form of the select statement for values of union types or anytype.
requirements.original: To allow easier usage of the select statement for values of union types or anytype, a special form of the select statement exists.

requirements.subject: ent:select-union-statement
requirements.canonical: The select union statement has the syntax `select union` "(" [(VarInstance | Assignment) ";"] SingleExpression ")" "{" followed by one or more branches `case` "(" ({Identifier [","]} | {TypeIdentifier [","]}) ")" StatementBlock, an optional `case else` StatementBlock, and a closing "}".
requirements.original:
select union "(" [(VarInstance|Assignment) ";"] SingleExpression ")" "{" 
     { case "(" ({ Identifier [","] } | { TypeIdentifier [","] }) ")" StatementBlock }+
     [ case else StatementBlock ]
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:select-union-statement
requirements.canonical: A select union statement IS composed of a header part and one or more branches.
requirements.original: The statement contains a header part and one or more branches.

requirements.subject: ent:select-union-statement
requirements.canonical: An execution of a select union statement SHALL NOT execute more than one of its branches.
requirements.original: Never more than one of the branches is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:header-part
requirements.canonical: The header part of a select union statement SHALL contain a template instance of a union type or of anytype.
requirements.original: In the header part of the select union statement a template instance of union type or anytype shall be given.

requirements.subject: ent:init-statement
requirements.canonical: The expression in the header of a select union statement MAY be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment).
requirements.original: The expression in the header may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:init-statement
requirements.canonical: The init statement of a select union statement IS executed before the header expression is evaluated.
requirements.original: The expression in the header may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: The scope of a variable declared within the init statement of a select union statement SHALL be limited to the select union statement.
requirements.original: The scope of variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the select union statement.

requirements.subject: ent:list-branch
requirements.condition: the header template instance has a union type
requirements.canonical: If the header template instance of a select union statement has a union type, each list branch SHALL start with the `case` keyword followed by one or more identifiers of alternatives (fields) of the union type.
requirements.original: If the template instance has a union type, each branch shall start with the case keyword followed by one or more identifiers of the alternatives (fields) of the union type (a list branch) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.condition: the header template instance has a union type
requirements.canonical: If the header template instance of a select union statement has a union type, the last branch MAY be an else branch consisting of `case else` and a statement block.
requirements.original: If the template instance has a union type, each branch shall start with the case keyword followed by one or more identifiers of the alternatives (fields) of the union type (a list branch) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:list-branch
requirements.condition: the header template instance has type anytype
requirements.canonical: If the header template instance of a select union statement has type anytype, each list branch SHALL start with the `case` keyword followed by one or more type names.
requirements.original: If the template instance has type anytype, each branch shall start with the case keyword followed by one or more type names (a list branch) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.condition: the header template instance has type anytype
requirements.canonical: If the header template instance of a select union statement has type anytype, the last branch MAY be an else branch consisting of `case else` and a statement block.
requirements.original: If the template instance has type anytype, each branch shall start with the case keyword followed by one or more type names (a list branch) or in the last branch the case keyword may be followed by the else keyword (an else branch) and a statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:list-branch
requirements.canonical: The statement block of the list branch containing the identifier or type identifier of the chosen alternative IS executed.
requirements.original: The StatementBlock of the list branch containing the identifier or type identifier of the chosen alternative is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.condition: no case exists for the chosen alternative and an else branch is present
requirements.canonical: If no case exists for the chosen alternative and an else branch is present, the statement block of the else branch IS executed.
requirements.original: If no case exists for the chosen alternative, the StatementBlock of the else branch, if it is present, is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:select-union-statement
requirements.condition: no case exists for the chosen alternative and no else branch is present
requirements.canonical: If no case exists for the chosen alternative and no else branch is present, the select union statement HAS no effect.
requirements.original: Otherwise, the select union statement has no effect.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression in the header of a select union statement SHALL be of a union type or anytype.
requirements.original: a) The SingleExpression in the header of the select union statement shall be of a union type.

ambiguity.issue: Restriction a) only mentions union types, while the semantic description and the example also allow anytype; chosen reading: anytype is included.
readings: The SingleExpression in the header of a select union statement SHALL be of a union type or anytype.
The SingleExpression in the header of a select union statement SHALL be of a union type only.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression in the header of a select union statement SHALL be at least partially initialized.
requirements.original: It shall be at least partially initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:case-keyword
requirements.canonical: Every Identifier in a case of a select union statement SHALL be the identifier of an alternative of the union type of the header template instance.
requirements.original: b) Every Identifier in a case of the select union statement shall be an identifier of an alternative of the union type of the template instance given to the statement's header.

requirements.subject: ent:case-keyword
requirements.canonical: Two cases of a select union statement SHALL NOT have the same case Identifier or TypeIdentifier.
requirements.original: c) No two cases in a select union statement shall have the same case Identifier or TypeIdentifier.

requirements.subject: ent:for-statement
requirements.canonical: The traditional form of the for statement IS a counter loop.
requirements.original: The traditional form of the for statement defines a counter loop.

requirements.subject: ent:for-statement
requirements.canonical: The counter loop for statement has the syntax `for` "(" (VarInstance | Assignment) ";" BooleanExpression ";" Assignment ")" StatementBlock.
requirements.original:
for "(" ( VarInstance | Assignment ) ";" BooleanExpression ";" Assignment ")"
       StatementBlock

requirements.subject: ent:for-statement
requirements.canonical: A counter loop for statement IS composed of two assignments and a boolean expression.
requirements.original: The for statement contains two assignments and a boolean expression.

ambiguity.issue: The syntax also allows a variable declaration (VarInstance) instead of the first assignment; chosen reading: 'assignment' includes a variable declaration with initialization.
readings: The first part of a for statement header IS an assignment or a variable declaration with initialization.
The first part of a for statement header IS always an assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment
requirements.canonical: The first assignment of a counter loop for statement SHALL initialize the index variable of the loop.
requirements.original: The first assignment is necessary to initialize the index (or counter) variable of the loop.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-expression
requirements.canonical: The boolean expression of a counter loop for statement IS the termination condition of the loop.
requirements.original: The boolean expression terminates the loop and the second assignment is used to manipulate the index variable.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment
requirements.canonical: The second assignment of a counter loop for statement IS used to manipulate the index variable.
requirements.original: The boolean expression terminates the loop and the second assignment is used to manipulate the index variable.

requirements.subject: ent:index-variable
requirements.canonical: The value of the index variable of a counter loop IS increased, decreased or manipulated such that a termination criterion is reached after a certain number of iterations.
requirements.original: The value of the index variable is increased, decreased or manipulated in such a manner that after a certain number of execution loops a termination criteria is reached.

ambiguity.issue: Unclear whether this describes the intended use or requires that every for loop terminates; chosen reading: descriptive.
readings: The index variable IS typically manipulated so that the loop terminates (descriptive).
The second assignment SHALL manipulate the index variable so that the loop terminates (obligation).

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-expression
requirements.canonical: The termination criterion of a counter loop for statement SHALL be expressed by a boolean expression.
requirements.original: The termination criterion of the loop shall be expressed by a boolean expression.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-expression
requirements.canonical: The termination criterion of a counter loop for statement IS checked at the beginning of each new loop iteration.
requirements.original: It is checked at the beginning of each new loop iteration.

requirements.subject: ent:for-statement
requirements.condition: the boolean expression evaluates to true
requirements.canonical: If the termination criterion of a counter loop for statement evaluates to true, execution continues with the statement block of the for statement.
requirements.original: If it evaluates to true, the execution continues with the statement block in the for statement, if it evaluates to false, the execution continues with the statement which immediately follows the for loop.

requirements.subject: ent:for-statement
requirements.condition: the boolean expression evaluates to false
requirements.canonical: If the termination criterion of a counter loop for statement evaluates to false, execution continues with the statement immediately following the for loop.
requirements.original: If it evaluates to true, the execution continues with the statement block in the for statement, if it evaluates to false, the execution continues with the statement which immediately follows the for loop.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.condition: the break statement is not within an enclosed loop, alt, altstep or interleave
requirements.canonical: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt statement, altstep or interleave statement, the for loop IS terminated.
requirements.original: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt, alststep or interleave, then the loop is terminated, too.

ambiguity.issue: The text uses the misspelling 'alststep' instead of 'altstep'.

requirements.subject: ent:index-variable
requirements.canonical: The index variable of a counter loop MAY be declared before being used in the for statement.
requirements.original: The index variable of a for loop can be declared before being used in the for statement or can be declared and initialized in the for statement header.

requirements.subject: ent:index-variable
requirements.canonical: The index variable of a counter loop MAY be declared and initialized in the for statement header.
requirements.original: The index variable of a for loop can be declared before being used in the for statement or can be declared and initialized in the for statement header.

requirements.subject: ent:index-variable
requirements.condition: the index variable is declared and initialized in the for statement header
requirements.canonical: If the index variable is declared and initialized in the for statement header, the scope of the index variable IS limited to the loop body.
requirements.original: If the index variable is declared and initialized in the for statement header, the scope of the index variable is limited to the loop body, i.e. it is only visible inside the loop body.

ambiguity.issue: The header's boolean expression and second assignment also reference the index variable; chosen reading: the scope covers the for statement header and the loop body but nothing outside the for statement.
readings: The index variable IS visible in the for statement header and the loop body only.
The index variable IS visible only inside the loop body (statement block).

requirements.subject: ent:range-based-loop
requirements.canonical: The range-based loop IS a for statement that iterates over the elements provided by a range expression.
requirements.original: The range-based loop iterates over the elements provided by a range expression.

requirements.subject: ent:range-based-loop
requirements.canonical: The range-based loop has the syntax `for` "(" [`var` TypeOrNestedTypeDef] ValueRef `in` Expression ")" StatementBlock.
requirements.original:
for "(" [ var TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] ValueRef in Expression ")"
      StatementBlock

requirements.subject: ent:range-expression
requirements.canonical: The range expression of a range-based loop IS evaluated exactly once before the loop begins.
requirements.original: The range expression is evaluated once before beginning the loop and may be partially initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:range-expression
requirements.canonical: The range expression of a range-based loop MAY be partially initialized.
requirements.original: The range expression is evaluated once before beginning the loop and may be partially initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:range-expression
requirements.canonical: The range expression of a range-based loop SHALL evaluate to a value whose root type is record of, set of, array, octetstring, hexstring, bitstring, charstring or universal charstring.
requirements.original: The range _expression shall evaluate to a value with root type record of, set of, array, octetstring, hexstring, bitstring,_ **charstring or universal charstring.**

ambiguity.issue: The list does not include map types, but NOTE 1 and EXAMPLE 3 iterate over map keys (m.from); chosen reading: map key/value projections count as record of / set of values.
readings: The range expression SHALL be of one of the listed root types, where map key and value projections (`.from`, `.to`) are regarded as set of values.
The range expression SHALL be of one of the listed root types only, so iteration over map keys or values is not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:range-based-loop
requirements.canonical: A range-based loop iterates over the elements of the range expression in sequential order.
requirements.original: Elements are iterated in sequential order.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.canonical: In each iteration of a range-based loop the corresponding element IS assigned to the iteration variable.
requirements.original: In each iteration the appropriate element is assigned to the iteration variable and the statement block is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:statement-block
requirements.canonical: In each iteration of a range-based loop the statement block IS executed after the element has been assigned to the iteration variable.
requirements.original: In each iteration the appropriate element is assigned to the iteration variable and the statement block is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.condition: the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header
requirements.canonical: If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, its scope and lifetime ARE limited to the statement block.
requirements.original: If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, its scope and lifetime is limited to the statement block, i.e. a new iteration variable is initialized in every iteration.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.condition: the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header
requirements.canonical: If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, a new iteration variable IS initialized in every iteration.
requirements.original: If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, its scope and lifetime is limited to the statement block, i.e. a new iteration variable is initialized in every iteration.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.condition: the iteration variable is declared outside the for statement
requirements.canonical: If the iteration variable is declared outside the for statement, its value after the execution of the loop IS that of the last iteration.
requirements.original: If the iteration variable is declared outside the for statement, after execution its value will be that of the last iteration.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.canonical: The assignment of an element to the iteration variable SHALL follow the assignment rules of clause 19.1.1.
requirements.original: The assignment to the iteration variable follows the rules specified in clause 19.1.1 with the exception that assignment of uninitialized elements is permitted.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.canonical: An uninitialized element MAY be assigned to the iteration variable of a range-based loop.
requirements.original: The assignment to the iteration variable follows the rules specified in clause 19.1.1 with the exception that assignment of uninitialized elements is permitted.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.condition: an uninitialized element is assigned
requirements.canonical: When an uninitialized value is assigned to the iteration variable, the iteration variable IS uninitialized.
requirements.original: When an uninitialized value is assigned to the iterator variable, the iterator variable becomes uninitialized.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence uses 'iterator variable' while the rest of the clause uses 'iteration variable'.

requirements.subject: ent:map-type
requirements.canonical: The iteration order of map keys and map values IS tool dependent and IS NOT guaranteed to be the same from one iteration to the next.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: The iteration order of map keys and map values is tool dependent and is not guaranteed to be the same from one iteration to the next.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.canonical: The behaviour of a lazy or fuzzy iteration variable IS NOT specified.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The behaviour of lazy or fuzzy iteration variables is not specified and should not be used to avoid future compatibility issues.

requirements.subject: ent:iteration-variable
requirements.canonical: A lazy or fuzzy iteration variable SHOULD NOT be used, to avoid future compatibility issues.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The behaviour of lazy or fuzzy iteration variables is not specified and should not be used to avoid future compatibility issues.

requirements.subject: ent:while-statement
requirements.canonical: A while statement IS a loop that is executed as long as the loop condition holds.
requirements.original: A while statement defines a loop that is executed as long as the loop condition holds.

requirements.subject: ent:while-statement
requirements.canonical: The while statement has the syntax `while` "(" [(VarInstance | Assignment) ";"] BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock.
requirements.original: while "(" [(VarInstance|Assignment) ";"] BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock

requirements.subject: ent:init-statement
requirements.canonical: The loop condition of a while statement MAY be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment).
requirements.original: The loop condition may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:init-statement
requirements.canonical: The init statement of a while statement IS executed before the loop condition is evaluated.
requirements.original: The loop condition may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

ambiguity.issue: Unclear whether the init statement executes once before the first evaluation or before every evaluation of the loop condition; chosen reading: once.
readings: The init statement of a while statement IS executed once, before the loop condition is evaluated for the first time.
The init statement of a while statement IS executed before each evaluation of the loop condition.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: The scope of a variable declared within the init statement of a while statement SHALL be limited to the while statement.
requirements.original: The scope of variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the while statement.

requirements.subject: ent:loop-condition
requirements.canonical: The loop condition of a while statement SHALL be checked at the beginning of each new loop iteration.
requirements.original: The loop condition shall be checked at the beginning of each new loop iteration.

requirements.subject: ent:while-statement
requirements.condition: the loop condition does not hold
requirements.canonical: If the loop condition of a while statement does not hold, the loop SHALL be exited and execution SHALL continue with the statement immediately following the while loop.
requirements.original: If the loop condition does not hold, then the loop is exited and execution shall continue with the statement, which immediately follows the while loop.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.condition: the break statement is not within an enclosed loop, alt, altstep or interleave
requirements.canonical: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt statement, altstep or interleave statement, the while loop IS terminated.
requirements.original: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt, alststep or interleave, then the loop is terminated, too.

ambiguity.issue: The text uses the misspelling 'alststep' instead of 'altstep'.

requirements.subject: ent:do-while-statement
requirements.canonical: A do-while statement IS a loop that is executed until the loop condition does not hold.
requirements.original: A do-while statement defines a loop that is executed up until the loop condition does not hold.

requirements.subject: ent:do-while-statement
requirements.canonical: The do-while statement has the syntax `do` StatementBlock `while` "(" BooleanExpression ")".
requirements.original: do StatementBlock while "(" BooleanExpression ")"

requirements.subject: ent:do-while-statement
requirements.canonical: A do-while loop IS identical to a while loop except for the point at which the loop condition is checked.
requirements.original: The do-while loop is identical to a while loop with the exception that the loop condition shall be checked at the end of each loop iteration.

requirements.subject: ent:loop-condition
requirements.canonical: The loop condition of a do-while statement SHALL be checked at the end of each loop iteration.
requirements.original: The do-while loop is identical to a while loop with the exception that the loop condition shall be checked at the end of each loop iteration.

requirements.subject: ent:do-while-statement
requirements.canonical: The statement block of a do-while loop IS executed at least once before the loop condition is evaluated for the first time.
requirements.original: This means when using a do-while loop the behaviour is executed at least once before the loop condition is evaluated for the first time.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.condition: the break statement is not within an enclosed loop, alt, altstep or interleave
requirements.canonical: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt statement, altstep or interleave statement, the do-while loop IS terminated.
requirements.original: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt, alststep or interleave, then the loop is terminated, too.

ambiguity.issue: The text uses the misspelling 'alststep' instead of 'altstep'.

requirements.subject: ent:label-statement
requirements.canonical: A label statement MAY be used in test cases, functions and altsteps.
requirements.original: The label statement allows the specification of labels in test cases, functions and altsteps.

requirements.subject: ent:label-statement
requirements.canonical: The label statement has the syntax `label` LabelIdentifier.
requirements.original: label LabelIdentifier

requirements.subject: ent:label
requirements.canonical: A label marks a statement.
requirements.original: A label marks a statement.

requirements.subject: ent:label
requirements.canonical: A label IS used by the goto statement to transfer control to the labelled statement.
requirements.original: The label is used by the goto statement (see clause 19.8) to transfer control to a labelled statement.

requirements.subject: ent:label-statement
requirements.canonical: A label statement MAY be used like any other TTCN-3 behavioural program statement according to the syntax rules of annex A.
requirements.original: a) A label statement can be used freely like other TTCN-3 behavioural program statements according to the syntax rules defined in annex A.

requirements.subject: ent:label-statement
requirements.canonical: A label statement MAY be placed before or after a TTCN-3 statement.
requirements.original: It can be used before or after a TTCN-3 statement

requirements.subject: ent:label-statement
requirements.canonical: A label statement SHALL NOT be the first statement of an alternative or top alternative in an alt statement, interleave statement or altstep.
requirements.original: but not as the first statement of an alternative or top alternative in an alt statement, interleave statement or altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:label
requirements.canonical: A label defined by a label statement SHALL be unique among all labels defined in the same test case, function or altstep.
requirements.original: b) Labels used following the label keyword shall be unique among all labels defined in the same test case, function or altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement performs a jump to a label.
requirements.original: A goto statement performs a jump to a label.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: The goto statement has the syntax `goto` LabelIdentifier.
requirements.original: goto LabelIdentifier

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement MAY be used in functions, test cases and altsteps to transfer control to a labelled statement.
requirements.original: The goto statement can be used in functions, test cases and altsteps to transfer control to a labelled statement.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement MAY jump forwards and backwards within a sequence of statements.
requirements.original: The goto statement provides the possibility to jump freely, i.e. forwards and backwards, within a sequence of statements, to jump out of a single compound statement (e.g. a while loop) and to jump over several levels out of nested compound statements (e.g. nested alternatives).

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement MAY jump out of a single compound statement.
requirements.original: The goto statement provides the possibility to jump freely, i.e. forwards and backwards, within a sequence of statements, to jump out of a single compound statement (e.g. a while loop) and to jump over several levels out of nested compound statements (e.g. nested alternatives).

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement MAY jump over several levels out of nested compound statements.
requirements.original: The goto statement provides the possibility to jump freely, i.e. forwards and backwards, within a sequence of statements, to jump out of a single compound statement (e.g. a while loop) and to jump over several levels out of nested compound statements (e.g. nested alternatives).

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement SHALL NOT jump out of a function, test case or altstep.
requirements.original: a) It is not allowed to jump out of or into functions, test cases and altsteps.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement SHALL NOT jump into a function, test case or altstep.
requirements.original: a) It is not allowed to jump out of or into functions, test cases and altsteps.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement SHALL NOT jump into a sequence of statements defined in a compound statement (alt statement, while loop, for loop, if-else statement, do-while loop or interleave statement).
requirements.original: b) It is not allowed to jump into a sequence of statements defined in a compound statement (i.e. alt statement, while loop, for loop, if-else statement, do-while loop and the interleave statement).

ambiguity.issue: The list introduced by 'i.e.' omits select case and select union statements and plain statement blocks; chosen reading: the list is exhaustive.
readings: A goto statement SHALL NOT jump into the statements of an alt, while, for, if-else, do-while or interleave statement only.
A goto statement SHALL NOT jump into any compound statement, including select case and select union statements.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement SHALL NOT be used within an interleave statement.
requirements.original: c) It is not allowed to use the goto statement within an interleave statement.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-statement
requirements.canonical: The `stop` statement SHALL terminate the execution of a test component, a test case or the control behaviour.
requirements.original: The stop statement terminates execution of test components, a test case or a test control.

ambiguity.issue: "test control" is used instead of the glossary term "control behaviour" (module control function).

requirements.subject: ent:stop-statement
requirements.canonical: The `stop` statement has the syntax `stop`.
requirements.original: stop

requirements.subject: ent:stop-statement
requirements.canonical: The `stop` statement terminates execution in different ways depending on the context in which it is executed.
requirements.original: The stop statement terminates execution in different ways depending on the context in which it is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-statement
requirements.condition: the stop statement is executed in a control behaviour
requirements.canonical: When executed in a control behaviour, the `stop` statement SHALL terminate the execution of the control component.
requirements.original: When executed in a control behaviour, it terminates the execution of the control component.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-statement
requirements.condition: the stop statement is invoked in a test case, altstep or function executed on a test component
requirements.canonical: When invoked in a test case, altstep or function executed on a test component, the `stop` statement SHALL terminate that test component.
requirements.original: When invoked in a test case, altstep or function that are executed on a test component, it terminates the relevant test component.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-statement
requirements.canonical: A `stop` statement that terminates a test component IS semantically identical to the stop component operation `self.stop`.
requirements.original: NOTE: The semantics of a stop statement that terminates a test component is identical to the stop component operation self.stop (see clause 21.3.3).

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: The `return` statement SHALL terminate the execution of a function or altstep.
requirements.original: The return statement terminates execution of functions or altsteps.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: The `return` statement has the syntax `return` optionally followed by an Expression or a TemplateInstance.
requirements.original: return [ Expression | TemplateInstance ]

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: The `return` statement SHALL return control to the point from which the function or altstep was called.
requirements.original: The return statement terminates execution of a function or altstep and returns control to the point from which the function or altstep was called.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.condition: the return statement is used in a function
requirements.canonical: A `return` statement used in a function MAY be associated with a return value or template.
requirements.original: When used in functions, a return statement may be optionally associated with a return value or template.

readings: A `return` statement in a function MAY be associated with a return value or template, and SHALL be so exactly when the function has a return clause.
A `return` statement in a function MAY be associated with a return value or template regardless of the function's return clause.
ambiguity.issue: "optionally" is read as depending on the return clause of the function (chosen, consistent with clause 16.1); it could also be read as an unconditional option.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: An altstep call within an `alt` statement MAY be followed by an optional statement block.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows optional statement blocks that may follow altstep calls within alt statements.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.condition: a statement block follows the altstep call within the alt statement
requirements.canonical: If a statement block follows the altstep call in an `alt` statement, the `return` statement in the altstep SHALL return control to the beginning of that statement block.
requirements.original: If there is a statement block, the return statement returns control to the beginning of this statement block and the statement block is executed before the alt statement is left.

requirements.subject: ent:statement-block
requirements.condition: a statement block follows the altstep call within the alt statement
requirements.canonical: If a statement block follows the altstep call in an `alt` statement and the altstep is left by a `return` statement, the statement block SHALL be executed before the `alt` statement is left.
requirements.original: If there is a statement block, the return statement returns control to the beginning of this statement block and the statement block is executed before the alt statement is left.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.condition: no statement block follows the altstep call within the alt statement
requirements.canonical: If no statement block follows the altstep call in an `alt` statement, test execution SHALL continue with the first statement following the `alt` statement after the `return` statement in the altstep is executed.
requirements.original: If there is no statement block, test execution continues with the first statement following the alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: The return value or template of a `return` statement SHALL be evaluated before control is returned.
requirements.original: The return value or template is first evaluated before returning.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: A `return` statement SHALL NOT be present in a testcase definition.
requirements.original: a) The return statement shall not be present in testcase definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The `log` statement provides the means to write logging information to some logging device.
requirements.original: The log statement provides the means to write logging information to some logging device.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a module parameter identifier as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: module parameter identifier; What is logged: actual value

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a module parameter identifier is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a module parameter identifier is used in a `log` statement, the actual value of the module parameter IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: module parameter identifier; What is logged: actual value

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a literal value as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: literal value; What is logged: value; Comment: This includes also free text.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a literal value is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a literal value is used in a `log` statement, the value IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: literal value; What is logged: value; Comment: This includes also free text.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A literal value used as a log item in a `log` statement IS allowed to be free text.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: literal value; What is logged: value; Comment: This includes also free text.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a data constant identifier as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: data constant identifier; What is logged: actual value

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a data constant identifier is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a data constant identifier is used in a `log` statement, the actual value of the constant IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: data constant identifier; What is logged: actual value

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a template instance as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: template instance; What is logged: actual template or field values and matching symbols

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a template instance is used in a log statement
