requirements.canonical: When a template instance is used in a `log` statement, the actual template or field values and matching symbols IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: template instance; What is logged: actual template or field values and matching symbols

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a variable identifier as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: variable identifier; What is logged: actual value or "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: See notes 3 and 4.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a variable identifier is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a variable identifier is used in a `log` statement, the actual value of the variable or "UNINITIALIZED" IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: variable identifier; What is logged: actual value or "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: See notes 3 and 4.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `self`, `mtc`, `system` or component type variable identifier as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: self, mtc, system or component type variable identifier; What is logged: actual value and if assigned the component instance name otherwise "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: On logging actual values see notes 2 to 4. Actual component states shall be logged according to note 5.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `self`, `mtc`, `system` or component type variable identifier is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `self`, `mtc`, `system` or component type variable identifier is used in a `log` statement, the actual value and, if assigned, the component instance name, otherwise "UNINITIALIZED" IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: self, mtc, system or component type variable identifier; What is logged: actual value and if assigned the component instance name otherwise "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: On logging actual values see notes 2 to 4. Actual component states shall be logged according to note 5.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a self, mtc, system or component type variable identifier is logged
requirements.canonical: When a `self`, `mtc`, `system` or component type variable identifier is logged, the actual component state SHALL be logged as one of Inactive, Running, Stopped or Killed.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: self, mtc, system or component type variable identifier; What is logged: actual value and if assigned the component instance name otherwise "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: On logging actual values see notes 2 to 4. Actual component states shall be logged according to note 5.

readings: The actual component state SHALL be logged in addition to the actual value and component instance name.
The actual component state SHALL be logged only when the component state is logged at all; the column only requires the value and instance name.
ambiguity.issue: The "What is logged" column does not mention the component state while the comment requires it; chosen reading: the state is logged in addition to the value and name.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `create` operation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: create operation; What is logged: actual state and the component instance name; Comment: The actual state is always set to Inactive.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `create` operation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `create` operation is used in a `log` statement, the actual state and the component instance name IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: create operation; What is logged: actual state and the component instance name; Comment: The actual state is always set to Inactive.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a create operation is logged
requirements.canonical: When a `create` operation is logged, the logged actual state IS always Inactive.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: create operation; What is logged: actual state and the component instance name; Comment: The actual state is always set to Inactive.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `running` operation (component or timer) as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: running operation (component or timer); What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false. In case of component or timer arrays, array element specification shall be included.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `running` operation (component or timer) is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `running` operation (component or timer) is used in a `log` statement, the return value (true or false) IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: running operation (component or timer); What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false. In case of component or timer arrays, array element specification shall be included.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: the `running` operation applies to an array
requirements.canonical: When a `running` operation on a component or timer array is logged, the array element specification SHALL be included.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: running operation (component or timer); What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false. In case of component or timer arrays, array element specification shall be included.

readings: A `running` operation used as log item on a component or timer array SHALL include the array element specification in the log statement argument.
The logged output of a `running` operation on an array SHALL include the array element specification.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether the array element specification has to be written in the log statement argument (a restriction) or included in the logged output; chosen reading: the argument shall contain the element specification.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain an `alive` operation (component) as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: alive operation (component); What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false. In case of arrays, array element specifications shall be included.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: an `alive` operation (component) is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When an `alive` operation (component) is used in a `log` statement, the return value (true or false) IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: alive operation (component); What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false. In case of arrays, array element specifications shall be included.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: the `alive` operation applies to an array
requirements.canonical: When a `alive` operation on a component or timer array is logged, the array element specification SHALL be included.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: alive operation (component); What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false. In case of arrays, array element specifications shall be included.

readings: A `alive` operation used as log item on a component or timer array SHALL include the array element specification in the log statement argument.
The logged output of a `alive` operation on an array SHALL include the array element specification.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether the array element specification has to be written in the log statement argument (a restriction) or included in the logged output; chosen reading: the argument shall contain the element specification.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `checkstate` operation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: checkstate operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `checkstate` operation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `checkstate` operation is used in a `log` statement, the return value (true or false) IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: checkstate operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a port instance as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: port instance; What is logged: actual state; Comment: Port states shall be logged according to note 6.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a port instance is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a port instance is used in a `log` statement, the actual state of the port IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: port instance; What is logged: actual state; Comment: Port states shall be logged according to note 6.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a port instance is logged
requirements.canonical: When a port instance is logged, the port state SHALL be logged as Started or Stopped.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: port instance; What is logged: actual state; Comment: Port states shall be logged according to note 6.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a default type variable identifier as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: default type variable identifier; What is logged: actual state or "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: Default states shall be logged according to note 7. See also notes 2 to 4.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a default type variable identifier is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a default type variable identifier is used in a `log` statement, the actual state of the default or "UNINITIALIZED" IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: default type variable identifier; What is logged: actual state or "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: Default states shall be logged according to note 7. See also notes 2 to 4.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a default type variable identifier is logged
requirements.canonical: When a default type variable identifier is logged, the default state SHALL be logged as Activated or Deactivated.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: default type variable identifier; What is logged: actual state or "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: Default states shall be logged according to note 7. See also notes 2 to 4.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain an `activate` operation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: activate operation; What is logged: activate operation; Comment: The actual state is always set to activated.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: an `activate` operation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When an `activate` operation is used in a `log` statement, the activate operation (its actual state) IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: activate operation; What is logged: activate operation; Comment: The actual state is always set to activated.

readings: When an `activate` operation is logged, the actual state of the resulting default (Activated) IS logged.
When an `activate` operation is logged, a textual representation of the activate operation itself IS logged.
ambiguity.issue: The "What is logged" column says "activate operation", which does not name a loggable item; chosen reading: the actual state of the activated default (comment: "always set to activated").

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: an activate operation is logged
requirements.canonical: When an `activate` operation is logged, the logged actual state IS always Activated.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: activate operation; What is logged: activate operation; Comment: The actual state is always set to activated.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a timer name as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: timer name; What is logged: actual state; Comment: Timer states shall be logged according to note 8.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a timer name is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a timer name is used in a `log` statement, the actual state of the timer IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: timer name; What is logged: actual state; Comment: Timer states shall be logged according to note 8.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a timer is logged
requirements.canonical: When a timer is logged, the timer state SHALL be logged as Inactive, Running or Expired.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: timer name; What is logged: actual state; Comment: Timer states shall be logged according to note 8.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `read` operation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: read operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: See clause 23.4.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `read` operation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `read` operation is used in a `log` statement, the return value IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: read operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: See clause 23.4.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `match` operation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: match operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `match` operation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `match` operation is used in a `log` statement, the return value (true or false) IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: match operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `valueof` operation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: valueof operation; What is logged: return value

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `valueof` operation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `valueof` operation is used in a `log` statement, the return value IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: valueof operation; What is logged: return value

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `getverdict` operation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: getverdict operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: none, pass, inconc, or fail.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `getverdict` operation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `getverdict` operation is used in a `log` statement, the return value (none, pass, inconc or fail) IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: getverdict operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: none, pass, inconc, or fail.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a predefined function invocation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: predefined functions; What is logged: return value; Comment: See annex C.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a predefined function invocation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a predefined function invocation is used in a `log` statement, the return value IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: predefined functions; What is logged: return value; Comment: See annex C.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a function instance as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: function instance; What is logged: return value; Comment: Only functions with return clause are allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a function instance is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a function instance is used in a `log` statement, the return value IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: function instance; What is logged: return value; Comment: Only functions with return clause are allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a function instance is used as log item
requirements.canonical: A function instance used as a log item in a `log` statement SHALL refer to a function with a return clause.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: function instance; What is logged: return value; Comment: Only functions with return clause are allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain an external function instance as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: external function instance; What is logged: return value; Comment: Only external functions with return clause are allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: an external function instance is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When an external function instance is used in a `log` statement, the return value IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: external function instance; What is logged: return value; Comment: Only external functions with return clause are allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: an external function instance is used as log item
requirements.canonical: An external function instance used as a log item in a `log` statement SHALL refer to an external function with a return clause.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: external function instance; What is logged: return value; Comment: Only external functions with return clause are allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The actual value or actual template logged by a `log` statement IS the value or template at the moment of the execution of the `log` statement.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Actual value/actual template is the value/template at the moment of the execution of the log statement.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The type of a value logged by a `log` statement IS tool dependent.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The type of the logged value is tool dependent.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: an array identifier without array element specification is logged
requirements.canonical: When an array identifier without array element specification is logged, the actual values of all array elements, and for component references the names of all array elements, SHALL be logged.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: In case of array identifiers without array element specification, actual values and for component references names of all array elements shall be logged.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The string "UNINITIALIZED" IS logged only if the log item is unbound (uninitialized).
requirements.original: NOTE 4: The string "UNINITIALIZED" is logged only if the log item is unbound (uninitialized).

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The component state logged by a `log` statement IS one of Inactive, Running, Stopped and Killed.
requirements.original: NOTE 5: Component states that can be logged are: Inactive, Running, Stopped and Killed (for further details see annex F).

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The port state logged by a `log` statement IS one of Started and Stopped.
requirements.original: NOTE 6: Port states that can be logged are: Started and Stopped (for further details see annex F).

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The default state logged by a `log` statement IS one of Activated and Deactivated.
requirements.original: NOTE 7: Default states that can be logged are: Activated and Deactivated.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The timer state logged by a `log` statement IS one of Inactive, Running and Expired.
requirements.original: NOTE 8: Timer states that can be logged are: Inactive, Running and Expired (for further details see annex F).

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The logging of the fields of structured values and templates IS NOT standardized, so the logged information of different TTCN-3 tools may differ.
requirements.original: NOTE 9: As the logging of the fields of structured values and templates is not standardized, tools supplied by different vendors may differ in the logged information.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The `log` statement has the syntax `log` followed by a parenthesized sequence of FreeText or TemplateInstance items, each optionally followed by a comma.
requirements.original: log "(" { ( FreeText | TemplateInstance ) [","] } ")"

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The `log` statement writes one or more log items to a logging device associated with the control behaviour or the test component in which the statement is used.
requirements.original: The log statement provides the means to write one or more log items to some logging device associated with the test control or the test component in which the statement is used.

ambiguity.issue: "test control" is used instead of the glossary term "control behaviour".

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The log items of a `log` statement SHALL be given as a comma-separated list in the argument of the `log` statement.
requirements.original: Items to be logged shall be identified by a comma-separated list in the argument of the log statement.

readings: Log items SHALL be separated by commas.
Log items MAY be written without separating commas, as allowed by the syntactical structure.
ambiguity.issue: The syntactical structure (19.11-s037) makes the comma optional ([","]), while the prose requires a comma-separated list; chosen reading: commas are required between log items.

requirements.subject: ent:log-item
requirements.canonical: A log item MAY be an individual language element specified in table 18 or an expression composed of such log items.
requirements.original: Log items may be individual language elements specified in table 18 or expressions composed of such log items.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The execution of a `log` statement SHOULD have no effect on the test behaviour.
requirements.original: It is strongly recommended that the execution of the log statement has no effect on the test behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.condition: the function is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: A function used in a `log` statement SHOULD NOT (explicitly or implicitly) change component variable values, port status or timer status.
requirements.original: In particular, functions used in a log statement should not (explicitly or implicitly) change component variable values, port or timer status, and should not change the value of any of its inout or out parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.condition: the function is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: A function used in a `log` statement SHOULD NOT change the value of any of its `inout` or `out` parameters.
requirements.original: In particular, functions used in a log statement should not (explicitly or implicitly) change component variable values, port or timer status, and should not change the value of any of its inout or out parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.canonical: A `break` statement SHALL cause the exit from a loop, from an altstep, or from an `alt` or `interleave` statement.
requirements.original: A break statement causes the exit from a loop, from an altstep or from an alt or interleave statement.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.canonical: The `break` statement has the syntax `break`.
requirements.original: break

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a formal parameter identifier as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: formal parameter identifier; What is logged: see comment column; Comment: Logging of actual parameters shall follow rules specified for the language elements they are substituting. In case of value parameters the actual parameter value, in case of template-type parameters the actual template or field values and matching symbols, in case of component type parameters the actual component reference, etc. shall be logged.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The logging of an actual parameter SHALL follow the rules specified for the language element it substitutes.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: formal parameter identifier; What is logged: see comment column; Comment: Logging of actual parameters shall follow rules specified for the language elements they are substituting. In case of value parameters the actual parameter value, in case of template-type parameters the actual template or field values and matching symbols, in case of component type parameters the actual component reference, etc. shall be logged.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a value parameter is logged
requirements.canonical: When a value formal parameter identifier is logged, the actual parameter value SHALL be logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: formal parameter identifier; What is logged: see comment column; Comment: Logging of actual parameters shall follow rules specified for the language elements they are substituting. In case of value parameters the actual parameter value, in case of template-type parameters the actual template or field values and matching symbols, in case of component type parameters the actual component reference, etc. shall be logged.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a template parameter is logged
requirements.canonical: When a template formal parameter identifier is logged, the actual template or field values and matching symbols SHALL be logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: formal parameter identifier; What is logged: see comment column; Comment: Logging of actual parameters shall follow rules specified for the language elements they are substituting. In case of value parameters the actual parameter value, in case of template-type parameters the actual template or field values and matching symbols, in case of component type parameters the actual component reference, etc. shall be logged.

ambiguity.issue: "template-type parameters" is used instead of "template parameters" (template parameterization).

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a component type parameter is logged
requirements.canonical: When a component type formal parameter identifier is logged, the actual component reference SHALL be logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: formal parameter identifier; What is logged: see comment column; Comment: Logging of actual parameters shall follow rules specified for the language elements they are substituting. In case of value parameters the actual parameter value, in case of template-type parameters the actual template or field values and matching symbols, in case of component type parameters the actual component reference, etc. shall be logged.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.canonical: On executing a `break` statement, the innermost, currently executed loop, `alt` statement or `interleave` statement SHALL be left.
requirements.original: On executing a break statement the innermost, currently executed loop, alt statement or interleave statement is left.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.canonical: After a `break` statement, execution SHALL continue with the statement following the construct which is left.
requirements.original: Execution continues with the statement following the construct which is left.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.canonical: A `break` statement SHALL NOT be used outside the body of a loop (`for`, `while`, `do-while`) or an alternative of an `alt` or `interleave` statement; such use SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Using break outside the body of a loop (for, while, do-while) or an alternative of an alt or interleave statement shall cause an error.

readings: A `break` statement SHALL NOT be used outside a loop body, an alternative of an `alt` or `interleave` statement, or a top alternative of an altstep; misuse is detected at compile time.
A `break` statement SHALL NOT be used outside a loop body or an alternative of an `alt` or `interleave` statement (altsteps excluded); misuse causes a runtime error.
ambiguity.issue: The list omits altsteps although 19.12-s001 and 19.12-s018 allow break in a top alternative of an altstep, and it does not say whether the error is a compile-time or runtime error; chosen reading: break in altstep top alternatives is allowed and misuse is a static error.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep IS always executed within a surrounding `alt` statement.
requirements.original: Altsteps are always executed within a surrounding alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.condition: the execution of a top alternative of an altstep ends with a break statement
requirements.canonical: If the execution of a top alternative of an altstep ends with a `break` statement, the altstep and the surrounding `alt` statement SHALL be left.
requirements.original: If the execution of a top alternative of an altstep (see clause 16.2.1) ends with a break statement, the altstep and the surrounding alt statement are left.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.condition: an altstep is left by a break statement
requirements.canonical: When an altstep is left by a `break` statement, execution SHALL continue with the statement following the surrounding `alt` statement.
requirements.original: Execution continues with the statement following the surrounding alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:statement-block
requirements.condition: the altstep is left by a break statement
requirements.canonical: An optional statement block following an altstep call in an `alt` statement IS NOT executed when the altstep is left by executing a `break` statement.
requirements.original: These statement blocks are not executed when the altstep is left by executing a break statement.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.condition: the optional statement block following the altstep call has to be executed
requirements.canonical: If the optional statement block following an altstep call has to be executed, the altstep SHALL be left with a `return` statement.
requirements.original: A return statement has to be used, if such an optional statement block has to be executed (see clause 19.10).

requirements.subject: ent:continue-statement
requirements.canonical: A `continue` statement SHALL cause the start of the next iteration of a loop.
requirements.original: A continue statement causes the start of the next iteration of a loop.

requirements.subject: ent:continue-statement
requirements.canonical: The `continue` statement has the syntax `continue`.
requirements.original: continue

requirements.subject: ent:continue-statement
requirements.canonical: On executing a `continue` statement, the subsequent statements of the body of the innermost, currently executed loop SHALL be skipped.
requirements.original: On executing a continue statement, the subsequent statements of the body of the innermost, currently executed loop are skipped and the next iteration starts.

requirements.subject: ent:continue-statement
requirements.canonical: On executing a `continue` statement, the next iteration of the innermost, currently executed loop SHALL start.
requirements.original: On executing a continue statement, the subsequent statements of the body of the innermost, currently executed loop are skipped and the next iteration starts.

requirements.subject: ent:continue-statement
requirements.canonical: A `continue` statement SHALL NOT be used outside the body of a loop (`for`, `while`, `do-while`); such use SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Using continue outside the body of a loop (for, while, do-while) shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:statement-block
requirements.canonical: A statement block MAY be used like a basic program statement to introduce a local scope in the flow of control of TTCN-3 behaviour.
requirements.original: Statement blocks can be used like basic program statements to introduce a local scope in the flow of control of TTCN-3 behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:statement-block
requirements.canonical: The declarations and statements in a statement block SHALL be executed sequentially in the order of their appearance.
requirements.original: The declarations and statements in a statement block are executed in the order of their appearance, i.e. sequentially.

requirements.subject: ent:statement-block
requirements.canonical: A statement block has the syntax "{" followed by any number of LocalDefinition or Statement elements followed by "}".
requirements.original: "{" { LocalDefinition | Statement } "}"

requirements.subject: ent:statement-block
requirements.canonical: A statement block IS a local scope unit.
requirements.original: A statement block defines a local scope unit.
